sections.translation: The **RTP** connection offers maximum quality and low latency, but requires **network configuration** at both ends (transmitter and receiver).\ It is ideal for **fixed installations** or locations with **known and controlled networks**. **Network prerequisites**\ Ensure you have defined the correct **IP/port** and have resolved **NAT / firewall / port forwarding** on the receiver. Without this preparation, the link may not be established. Turn the **encoder** to **CONNECTION CENTER** and press it to enter the connection options. Choose **RTP STREAM** and press to open the RTP link screen (enable/disable). Select **YES** to start the RTP link to the studios. When active, the **CONNECTION CENTER** and **HOME** screens show **RTP STREAM ENABLED**. Repeat the procedure and select **NO** to disable the RTP. Before starting, verify that the **network and audio format configuration** on the MX2200 matches what is expected by the receiver (destination IP, **port**, **codec**, and **sample rate**). The **RTP transmission is unidirectional**. Return is typically not used in this mode because the location generates the content without interaction with the studio. If you need a **return** (intercom or floor), use **a SIP call** or a **telephone communication** (Bluetooth mobile phone or POTS land line) in parallel with the RTP. To receive the streaming from an MX2200 on a **computer**, use software with **RTP** support. **VLC Player** (free) is recommended. Configure the MX2200 with a format that the receiver supports directly: - **PCM16 @ 44.1 kHz** (linear) - **MP3** (any of the available modes) **OPUS** requires an **SDP (Session Description)** file to describe the content to the player. In **VLC Player**, go to **Media → Open Network Stream**. Use the format: ``` [protocol]://[source_IP]:[port] ``` Example: ``` rtp://0.0.0.0:3030 ``` Where: - `rtp` is the protocol used by the MX2200. - `0.0.0.0` indicates "**listen from any incoming IP**" on the receiving PC. - `3030` is the **port** configured for reception. Some versions of VLC also accept: `rtp://@:3030` Ensure the configured **UDP port** is **allowed** in the system firewall and the studio router's firewall.
